html:
The Tano, or Southern Tewa, were a Pueblo people of the Galisteo Basin, south of Santa Fe in New Mexico. They lived in large stone and adobe towns such as San Cristóbal, San Lázaro and Galisteo, farming maize with the help of the scarce water.

Spanish colonists of New Spain settled New Mexico from 1598 and put the Tano towns under missions and labour demands. The Tano were among the leaders of the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, which drove the Spanish out, and they moved into Santa Fe itself.

When the Spanish returned under Diego de Vargas in the 1690s, many Tano fled west. Some settled on First Mesa among the Hopi, where their descendants, the Hopi-Tewa, still live in the village of Hano and still speak Tewa. Their old towns in the Galisteo Basin were left empty.
